issues.legal_issue: A court exercising appellate jurisdiction may take account of material events that occur after proceedings begin when shaping relief.
material_facts: During the pending rent-control eviction proceedings, the landlord came into possession of another non-residential accommodation in the same town.
The statutory condition for the claimed eviction ground required that the landlord not be occupying a non-residential building in the town.
The later-acquired accommodation was brought to the High Court’s attention and materially affected the landlord’s entitlement to eviction.
issues.conclusion: The High Court was entitled to consider the subsequent event in deciding the eviction claim.
issues.legal_principle: Although entitlement to relief is ordinarily assessed as of the institution of proceedings, a court may—and in appropriate cases must—cautiously consider subsequent events that materially affect the right to relief or the way relief should be moulded, provided fairness to both sides is preserved. Procedure is the handmaid of justice, and this power is not confined to the trial court. The Court relied on Lachmeshwar Prasad Shukul v. Keshwar Lal Chaudhuri, which referred to Patterson v. State of Alabama and Minnesota v. National Tea Co. The later accommodation was material under section 10(3)(iii) of the Andhra Pradesh Buildings (Lease, Rent and Eviction) Control Act, 1960.

rule.if: rent_control_eviction_proceeding and material_post_filing_event and event_brought_to_court and fairness_preserved

predicates.rent_control_eviction_proceeding: The matter is a proceeding seeking eviction under rent-control law.
predicates.material_post_filing_event: A fact arose after the proceeding began that materially affects entitlement to relief or the form of relief.
predicates.event_brought_to_court: A party brought the subsequent event to the court’s attention.
predicates.fairness_preserved: The parties are afforded fairness in the court’s consideration of the subsequent event.

issues.definition: When a material event arising after a rent-control eviction proceeding begins is brought to the court’s attention and fairness is preserved, an appellate court may consider that event.

issues.legal_issue: An eviction proceeding need not be ended outright when a subsequent event defeats the ground originally pleaded but another legally permissible ground may be raised by amendment.
material_facts: The landlord’s acquisition of another non-residential accommodation during the proceeding disabled him from pursuing eviction on the ground originally invoked.
The High Court had made an adverse finding about that disability, and the Supreme Court held that the finding could not be reopened.
The litigation had already been prolonged, and the landlord might have another legally permissible ground for eviction.
The parties could be given an opportunity to file additional pleadings and lead evidence on any permitted amended ground.
issues.conclusion: The revision was to stand dismissed, but the eviction proceeding was not to be terminated outright: the Rent Controller was to take account of the established disability, the landlord could amend the petition on another legally permissible ground, and both sides were to have a fair opportunity to plead and present evidence. The established finding of disability could not be reopened.
issues.legal_principle: To avoid driving parties into new litigation of unknown duration, the court may mould relief to promote substantial justice while preserving fairness to both sides. The statutory disability arising under section 10(3)(iii) of the Andhra Pradesh Buildings (Lease, Rent and Eviction) Control Act, 1960 had to be taken into account, but other legally permissible grounds could be pursued through amendment with a fair opportunity for further pleadings and evidence.

rule.if: rent_control_eviction_proceeding and later_event_defeats_pleaded_ground and another_legal_ground_may_be_available and fair_opportunity_for_amendment_and_evidence

predicates.rent_control_eviction_proceeding: The matter is a proceeding seeking eviction under rent-control law.
predicates.later_event_defeats_pleaded_ground: A fact arising during the proceeding makes the ground originally pleaded unavailable.
predicates.another_legal_ground_may_be_available: The party seeking eviction may have another legally permissible ground to pursue.
predicates.fair_opportunity_for_amendment_and_evide: The parties can be given a fair opportunity to amend pleadings and present evidence on the permitted ground.

issues.definition: If a later event defeats the pleaded ground in a rent-control eviction proceeding but another legal ground may be available, the proceeding continues with a fair opportunity for amendment and evidence while the established disability finding remains preserved.
